environment.description: Same binary deployed on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement module 'terraform_provider_excloud_t'. The module confines the process to type 'terraform_provider_excloud_t' which has limited network permissions via 'corenet_tcp_connect_http_port' boolean and file access restricted to 'terraform_provider_excloud_var_t' labeled paths. Additionally, an AppArmor-like seccomp-bpf profile (loaded via systemd SecurityFilter) restricts the connect() syscall to only resolve to 127.0.0.0/8 and the specific OAuth endpoint IP (resolved at unit start via ExecStartPre). The token cache write path is confined but the critical control is that outbound redirects containing tokens cannot reach attacker-controlled hosts because the seccomp filter blocks connect() to non-whitelisted destinations, and the SELinux policy denies 'tcp_connect' to any port_type not in the provider's allowed set.

config.selinux_network_permissions: corenet_tcp_connect_http_port limited to auth.example.com:443 via nodecon and portcon rules
config.file_access: SELinux allows read/write only to terraform_provider_excloud_var_t, denies all other file types
